publication.name: I Tried Everything So You Don't Have To

posts.title: The Scale
posts.excerpt: Growing up, I was the husky kid. That’s what they called it. Husky . You know what that means. Just a nicer word for fat.
bold_lines: Husky
240 pounds
shame
boring, consistent, and done
system

posts.title: The Shamrock
posts.excerpt: I made the decision before January 2nd. That’s the part that matters and the part most people get wrong. They think you need to feel ready. You don’t. You pick the program, you commit to it, and then January 2nd is just the day…
bold_lines: You just go.
Thirty-six missed calls.
Distraught.
system

posts.title: Feelings Are Data
posts.subtitle: Not Directions
posts.excerpt: Young men get handed three emotional settings and told that’s the whole toolkit.
bold_lines: For me.
miscalibrated.
That’s the whole game.
You drive.

posts.title: The Chaos Test
posts.subtitle: Chicken and Broccoli
posts.excerpt: I wrote about the number. 240. The scale in the doctor’s office, the shame, the decision. If you read that, you know what happened next: chicken thighs, broccoli, butter. Every meal. Every day. The most boring system I could…
bold_lines: Four fractures. Facial and skull, including the one pushing her jaw out of alignment.
losing you.
It knows where I live.
There is no right time. There’s just time.

posts.title: The Loss of Leadership
posts.subtitle: The Legend of Zelda
posts.excerpt: I was ten years old when I conquered the original Legend of Zelda. Took me a month. Every day after school, alone in my room, no guide, no help, just the game and me. I got stuck constantly. I’d hit a wall and want to throw the…
bold_lines: I’m a builder.
Tell them why.
It’s even better to win as a team.

posts.title: The Thinking Partner
posts.subtitle: Rubber Ducky
posts.excerpt: Not like “kind of fast.” I mean the specific kind of fast where I watch someone’s eyes glaze over and realize I’ve been three topics ahead for the last two minutes. Where I’m iterating an idea out loud and the person across from…
bold_lines: It’s so lonely at times.

I’d bounce ideas off anyone who would listen. Friends, coworkers, my wife. I’d talk through a problem, hear myself say something that triggered the next thought, refine it, loop back, say it again slightly differently. People accused me of talking in circles. I wasn’t. I was iterating. I was rubber ducking with human beings who didn’t know that’s what was happening, and it overwhelmed them.
Nothing was wrong with me. The right system just didn’t exist yet.
The governor is off. Go build your house.

posts.title: Meet Claude
posts.subtitle: Cornered at a Party
posts.excerpt: The one who corners you at a party and just has so many words. The backstory. The side quests. A callback to something they mentioned twenty minutes ago. You’ve already forgotten. Your brain ran out of room.
bold_lines: That person is you.
Too much context and Claude forgets. Not enough context and Claude can’t deliver.
The tool will teach you how to use the tool.
Don’t mistake infinite patience for infinite memory.

posts.title: The Garage Gym
posts.subtitle: Lemonade
posts.excerpt: In the fall of 2013 my doctor told me my testosterone was 300.
bold_lines: The consistency was the goal.
I do.
When life throws punches, make lemonade.

posts.title: Totaling the Prius
posts.subtitle: The Blazer
posts.excerpt: I bought a Toyota Prius in June of 2006 because of a loophole.
bold_lines: I bought a black felt blazer.
You look better now than when you left the house.
My brain was already three moves ahead while my body was still on move one.
Why replace your coat when you can get a blazer?

posts.title: Disagree and Commit
posts.subtitle: The Bad Idea
posts.excerpt: February 2023. I just had my first colonoscopy. Procedure went fine. They told me three things before they let me leave: don’t sign any legal documents, don’t operate heavy machinery, and don’t make any major life decisions.
bold_lines: The kind of cute that makes the argument you just had feel stupid.
The rules you set before you love something don’t survive contact with actually loving it.
I took ownership of something I didn’t choose, and the ownership became the relationship.
The love follows the labor. It always does.

posts.title: freeIpods.com
posts.subtitle: Minus Two-Thirds
posts.excerpt: For three weeks, I slept with my laptop. Not on the nightstand, in the bed, close enough to grab without opening my eyes. The site had taken off like a rocket ship and the servers were buckling under the pressure, and I was the…
bold_lines: it couldn’t be me
There wasn’t one.
Competence doesn’t buy you safety.
The floor gave out. I just kept getting up.

posts.title: A House to Live In
posts.subtitle: The Keys
posts.excerpt: Recently I built a house for a guy named Bob.
bold_lines: I just don’t do it for me.
The house I kept refusing to live in was me.
the only house you ever live in is the one you never stop building.
Finally.

posts.title: Claude Chat, Claude Code, and Me
posts.subtitle: The Rocinante
posts.excerpt: I got tired of saying “Claude Chat” and “Claude Code.”
bold_lines: The session is temporary. The repo is permanent.
Something was missing.
The Lego bricks are waiting to be assembled.

posts.title: The Emulation Layer
posts.subtitle: No solutions, only trade-offs
posts.excerpt: I’m uncomfortable writing about this. And for some reason, I can’t shake the feeling that I must.
bold_lines: I have traits many would describe as autistic.
That distinction doesn’t survive the room.
Blessing and curse in the same circuit. No off switch.
This one was painful. I did it anyway.

posts.title: The Master Control Project
posts.subtitle: Hands of the Villain
posts.excerpt: Recently I had a conversation with my oldest friend. We talk fairly regularly. Some of it is the gym, what he’s lifting, what I’m lifting, who’s winning that particular argument this month. Some of it is life, his kids, my kids,…
bold_lines: the things that take extra effort are the ones you lose.
The filing had become the work.
How Bob worked
Why Master Control is different
How the capture actually works
The work was never the sorting. It was building the hands to do it.

posts.title: The Memory Problem
posts.subtitle: The Messy Parts
posts.excerpt: Every time I start a new conversation, the thing on the other side knows the sketch of me. My name, a few facts I have told it, some of what we have discussed before. What it does not have is depth. It does not know what we…
bold_lines: Humans do not think in documents.
This time I did not start over.
I rebuilt it five times. I finally used it.

posts.title: Model Context Protocol
posts.subtitle: The Tool Belt
posts.excerpt: For many years I’ve told people a REST API is a website for machines. And for just as long, the flip side came free: a website is an API for humans. It’s a good line.
bold_lines: A model that already reasons better than the code I was writing to reason for it.
The client got smart. My intuition is still catching up,
You can’t blindly trust your gut. AI is moving faster than your intuition.

posts.title: The Simplest System
posts.subtitle: Yellow Alert
posts.excerpt: I tell people I bought the giant yellow Yeti to fix two forms of memory loss. It reminds me to drink the water. And when I misplace it, it’s easy to spot.
bold_lines: I leave things places. My whole life.
“Very easy. Bright yellow.”
The load doesn’t get managed. It gets removed.
Just don’t pick yellow. That’s mine.

posts.title: Confidence Man
posts.subtitle: Distrust and Verify
posts.excerpt: I asked Fred to update a configuration and restart a service. Fred was the agent that lived on my Mac mini, the one I mentioned at the end of the Rocinante story . He reported back that it was done, and he included proof: the ID…
bold_lines: a lie with no liar behind it
the mark is whoever stops checking
“You still do that shit.”
“I would never.”

posts.title: Hand-Crafted with AI
posts.subtitle: Mistaken Identity
posts.excerpt: More than once, Erin has read a text message from me and asked if I used AI to write it. The time I remember best was an apology, the kind you send after an argument when you want to get it right. Measured. Careful. Every word…
bold_lines: I don’t type the words in these stories. Not one of them.
She was wrong about which one of us wrote it.

posts.title: The Day I Killed Fred
posts.subtitle: With Lasers
posts.excerpt: A while back, I wrote about my AI crew in Claude Chat, Claude Code, and Me . Buried in there was a line I never explained: “One of the crew has been reconfigured.” This is that story.
bold_lines: I built Fred to learn. I learned. So I adapted.
I discovered I didn’t need him anywhere.
The power was never in it knowing more. It was in knowing less.
And that’s the day I killed Fred with lasers.

posts.title: Wisdom Removed
posts.subtitle: I can’t walk, but I can run.
posts.excerpt: On the way home from the oral surgeon, Fiona asked for her favorite song. She’s fourteen. At check-in I’d told the front desk we were there to have her wisdom removed, and now the job was done: four wisdom teeth out under general…
bold_lines: she still opted out at the right time.
And here was the result of systems that Fiona built for herself.
Who you are when you can’t think is who you’ve been programming yourself to be.
You’re not everyone. You’re Fiona.

posts.title: Drinking from the Garden Hose
posts.subtitle: Potable Information
posts.excerpt: In January 2025 the water plant that serves our part of Virginia went dark. A winter storm took the power, the backups didn’t hold, the rooms with the equipment in them flooded, and the plant stopped making water. Richmond and…
bold_lines: The tap water was pool water.
Potable water
Potable information
Let it act. Give it something fit to act on.
The machine didn’t remove the bottleneck. It moved it, from reading to signing.
Potable water to drink. Potable information to act.

posts.title: The Effort of Being a Team
posts.subtitle: Trust the Awesomeness
posts.excerpt: There’s always a lot to get done as a family. Groceries, chores, appointments, who’s picking up whom. What is a family, if not an agile team: people who depend on each other to get real things done, on a schedule, together,…
bold_lines: A family agent, built because I could build it.
That’s what she thought to do with it. That’s the valuable part.
“I’ll block him.”
Time is the asset. Attention is how you spend it.

posts.title: Montana
posts.subtitle: The Escape Artist
posts.excerpt: Monday, August 24th, I took the day off work.
bold_lines: No one assigned her that job. She took it herself,
Same dog, start to finish.
What it got her was people, more of them than any of us expected, right when it counted.
Adventurous spirit. Kind soul.

posts.title: The Man Behind the Curtain
posts.subtitle: Rescuing Saint-14
posts.excerpt: Saturday morning I sat down to work on Skippy, and the first thing I do is check whether anyone actually used him that week.
bold_lines: Nothing went out.
It also stung.
Fiona is his favorite.
Talking to your customers still beats a design doc. And welcome to the family, Saint-14.

posts.title: Big Ideas
posts.subtitle: Expensive Production
posts.excerpt: Somewhere in the move into leadership, the read on me changed. Big ideas, smart, and they don’t always get implemented.
bold_lines: Making that happen is the job.
I made the same assumption about myself, which is worse, because I had all the information.
Thin is the wrong word. It’s slow.
Every single Tuesday. Six months and counting.

posts.title: Taking a Walk
posts.subtitle: Leading Yourself
posts.excerpt: A sinus infection took me out for a couple of days, right in the middle of an unusually rough work week. Being sick drained my energy and made my sleep worse. Last month, we also said goodbye to our dog, Montana . That grief…
bold_lines: It can feel like you’re taking a walk by yourself.
You don’t have to believe in the path to walk it.
It’s part of the job.
Leaders bring the weather. They also feel the rain.

posts.title: I Am the Root
posts.subtitle: Not How Facts Work
posts.excerpt: One evening in August, my wife Erin and I were hanging out, spending some quality time together, listening to music on the couch. It was the weekend. We’d had a few drinks, and she was texting on her phone. At some point she…
bold_lines: Skippy:
Erin:
or are we still fully committed to the coup?
that’s not how facts work, even by decree.
In our house it’s configured, ahead of time, on purpose.
Well played, Erin. Gold star, Skippy.

posts.title: Even AI Needs the Why
posts.subtitle: Head, Heart, and Hand
posts.excerpt: There’s an old idea in education that you teach the whole person: head, heart, and hand. It’s credited to Johann Heinrich Pestalozzi, a Swiss educator who was writing in those terms by 1805. He was talking about children in a…
bold_lines: A loose vision gets expensive quickly.
It’s one of the biggest mistakes I’ve made in my career.
The why brings trust, and trust is the foundation of resolve.
Everything has changed. Nothing is different.

posts.title: Claude Was Wrong
posts.subtitle: A New Primitive
posts.excerpt: I watched a video this week from a developer with a big YouTube following. His complaint about building with AI landed close to home. The machine never stops to ask whether the thing you want is a good idea. It builds what you…
bold_lines: It means one thing.
Good rules. Wrong problem.
the scarce skill is seeing where the parts go
Smarter than me. Not always right.

posts.title: The Whole Haystack
posts.subtitle: In Case I Need It
posts.excerpt: I asked my research library a question this week and had the answer in about three seconds. Links, dates, and the exact wording from sources I’d already read, listened to, or watched. Getting the same thing out of a deep research…
bold_lines: It outperformed us on evidence.
Information doesn’t take up space, but it still causes clutter.
Instead, we kept everything.
Save the whole haystack. Find the needles later.

posts.title: Rage Against the Machine
posts.subtitle: It Makes You Dumber
posts.excerpt: My daughter Alannah came home from Virginia Tech this summer after her freshman year. She’s a PPE major: philosophy, politics, and economics, studied together. Tech describes it as a way to take on some of the biggest social,…
bold_lines: So Alannah may have been more correct than she even realized.
Judging what an AI hands you is a different skill from judging what a person hands you.
I never did sit down with Alannah.
Stop mashing the keys. Start playing music.

posts.title: Who’s Driving?
posts.subtitle: The Blank
posts.excerpt: Every Sunday night a bot named Charles writes my wife a brief about our daughter’s week.
bold_lines: The house caught its own mistake before I knew there was one.
To a machine, a fact no one recorded looks like a job no one took.
And the house had already reported both, to me, and I hadn’t read that either.
Nobody assigned. That’s me.
